correctness.rationale: Over characteristic 3, setting u=x0,v=x2,a=x0−x1,b=x2−x3 gives F=ua³−vb³. The Jacobian ideal (a³,b³) has singular support L=(a,b); the affine ring R=k[t³,z,tz] on v≠0 has normalization B=k[t,z], finite birational, and conductor z²B=(a²,ab,b²)R by monomial semigroup membership. The projective bundle P(O(3)⊕O(1))≅F2 parameterizes normalization via [λ t³:λ s³:μs:μt], restricts to characteristic-three Frobenius on the nonnormal section, and is finite universal homeomorphism. For any geometric line outside two directrices, ratios (a:b) and (u:v) are linked by degree-3 Frobenius but each given by at most degree-one linear forms on a line, forcing constant ratios and a unique ruling line; ruling fibers disjoint. Finite-field rational points partition into two directrices and q+1 rational rulings, giving (q+1)^2; independent full projective point enumeration gave q=3:16, q=9:100, q=27:784.
residual_risks: The morphism section description uses projective bundle local trivializations; the affine conductor proof determines the global ideal along the singular line.
Classification is of geometric lines as sets, not scheme-theoretic relative Hilbert scheme or stable reduction.
